question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. When this extra water vapour condenses into precipitation, it results in heavier rain — or, if it's cold enough, heavier snow.
B. The atmosphere can store an additional 4% of water vapour for every additional 1°F of warming.
C. More water evaporates from soils, plants, lakes and seas as the atmosphere warms.
D. One of the most obvious indications of climate change is heavier rainfall.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. DCBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence D is the best opener because it introduces the general topic — heavier rainfall as an obvious indication of climate change.

• Sentence C logically follows D because it explains the underlying process: more water evaporates from soils, plants, lakes and seas as the atmosphere warms.

• Sentence B follows C because it gives the specific scientific fact that supports the evaporation idea — the atmosphere can store 4% more water vapour for every 1°F rise.

• Sentence A is the logical conclusion, stating the result of this stored extra water vapour — heavier rain or snow when it condenses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. DCBA.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (CBDA) is incorrect because it starts with C, which discusses evaporation without first introducing the topic of climate change and rainfall (D).

• Option 3 (ACDB) is incorrect because it starts with A, the concluding idea (condensation causing heavier rain), before the topic has even been introduced.

• Option 4 (BCAD) is incorrect because it starts with the specific scientific fact (B) before establishing the general topic (D) and the evaporation process (C).

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always look for the sentence that introduces the general topic — it is usually the opening sentence.

• Look for linking words, pronouns and logical cause-effect relationships (such as "this extra water vapour" in sentence A, which refers back to sentence B) to fix the correct sequence.

• Practise identifying whether a paragraph follows a general-to-specific or cause-to-effect structure, as most SSC para-jumble passages follow one of these patterns.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
She said, “I am in no mood to work now.”
option_1: She said that she has been in no mood to work then.
option_2: She said that she was in no mood to work now.
option_3: She said that she was in no mood to work then.
option_4: She said that she has been in no mood to work now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She said that she was in no mood to work then.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reporting verb "said" is in the past tense, and the reported speech is in the Simple Present form "am in no mood to work now", so the tense must be backshifted while converting to indirect speech.

• Rule — Narration change: When the reporting verb is in the past tense, present tense in direct speech changes to past tense in indirect speech. "am" changes to "was" (the pronoun "I" changes to "she" as per the subject, and the verb agrees with "she").

• Rule — Change of time/place words: The word "now" (used for present time) changes to "then" in indirect speech, since the reporting is happening at a later time.

• Applying both rules: "I am in no mood to work now" becomes "she was in no mood to work then."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "has been" is not the correct backshift of the Simple Present "am"; the correct backshift is simply "was".

• Option 2 is incorrect because it retains "now" instead of changing it to "then", even though the tense "was" has correctly been backshifted.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it incorrectly uses "has been" instead of "was", and also retains "now" instead of "then" — both required changes have been missed.

NOTE

• Common time/place word changes in narration: now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the previous day, here → there, this → that.

• Tense backshift chart: Simple Present → Simple Past; Present Continuous → Past Continuous; Present Perfect → Past Perfect; Simple Past → Past Perfect.

• Modal changes: can → could, will → would, may → might, must → had to.

question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
Manu will tell her later.
option_1: She will be tell later by Manu.
option_2: She will tell later by Manu.
option_3: She will be told later by Manu.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She will be told later by Manu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Manu will tell her later" is in the Simple Future Tense, in the active voice.

• Rule — Simple Future Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "her" becomes the subject "She"; the auxiliary "will be" is used; the verb "tell" becomes the past participle "told"; and "Manu" becomes the agent with "by".

• Passive: She will be told later by Manu.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will be tell" wrongly uses the base form "tell" instead of the past participle "told" after "be".

• Option 2 is incorrect because it omits the auxiliary "be" altogether — "will tell" is an active construction, not passive.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it drops the agent "by Manu" and also fails to use the past participle "told"; the doer of the action must be retained here since it is a named, meaningful agent.

NOTE

• In the passive voice, the main verb always takes its third form (V3), regardless of tense.

• The agent ("by + doer") may be dropped only when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant — here "Manu" is a specific, relevant agent and must be retained.

question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
Has the villa been occupied by them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Have they occupied the villa?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Has the villa been occupied by them?" is an interrogative sentence in the Present Perfect Tense (passive voice).

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense (interrogative):
◦ Passive: Has/Have + Subject + been + V3 + by + Agent + ?
◦ Active: Has/Have + Agent + V3 + Object + ?

• Applying the rule: the agent "them" becomes the subject "they"; the auxiliary "Has" changes to "Have" to agree with the plural subject "they"; the past participle "occupied" is retained as the main verb; and "the villa" becomes the object.

• Active: Have they occupied the villa?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "Did ... occupied" wrongly mixes the Simple Past auxiliary "Did" with the past participle "occupied" instead of the base form; this also changes the tense from Present Perfect to Simple Past.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "Had" is the auxiliary of the Past Perfect Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "Do ... occupied" wrongly mixes the Simple Present auxiliary "Do" with the past participle instead of the base form "occupy", and also changes the tense.

NOTE

• When converting an interrogative passive sentence to active voice, the auxiliary verb must agree in tense and number with the new subject (the former agent).

• Common mistake: mixing auxiliaries from one tense with the main verb form of another tense — always keep the tense of the auxiliary and the form of the main verb consistent.

question:
In the given sentence, one word may have been incorrectly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word from the given alternatives. If there is no error, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
The erroneous information spread rapidly across the nation and created a stir.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "erroneous", as printed in the given sentence, is already correctly spelt. It means containing errors, incorrect or mistaken.

• Spelling key: ERR + ONE + OUS. Remember the double "r" at the start (from the root "err", meaning to make a mistake) and the ending "-eous", not "-ious" or "-uous".

• Since none of the given alternative spellings match the correct spelling, and the word as printed is already correct, the appropriate answer is "No error".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "erronous" — incorrect; it drops one of the two "e"s before "ous", omitting a syllable of the word.

• Option 3: "eronneous" — incorrect; it has only a single "r" at the start and an extra "n" before "eous", both wrongly placed.

• Option 4: "errauneous" — incorrect; it inserts an extra letter "a" that does not belong in the word at all.

NOTE

• Related words: error (noun), err (verb), erroneously (adverb).

• Other commonly confused "-eous" ending words in SSC exams: courteous, righteous, spontaneous, simultaneous, advantageous.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘SINKS’ from the given sentence.
Groups work together to create Christmas parade themes, which are then carried out in floats, musical groups, and strolling figures.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Floats.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Sinks" means to descend or go down, especially below the surface of a liquid, or to decline/drop. (डूबना)
◦ Example: A heavy stone sinks quickly in water.

• The word "Floats", found in the given sentence, means to rest or move on or near the surface of a liquid without sinking, which is the direct opposite of "sinks". (तैरना)
◦ Example: A cork floats on water because it is lighter than water.

• Since "sinks" (to go down/submerge) and "floats" (to stay on the surface) describe opposite physical actions, "Floats" is the correct antonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Create" means to make or produce something; it is unrelated to the up/down motion implied by "sinks" and is not its opposite.

• Option 3: "Parade" refers to a public procession or march; it has no direct relation to the meaning of "sinks".

• Option 4: "Strolling" means walking in a slow, relaxed manner; it describes a type of movement but is not the opposite of "to sink".

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs frequently tested by SSC: rise ↔ sink/fall, ascend ↔ descend, emerge ↔ submerge, buoyant ↔ heavy.

• In this question format, the four options are words already present in the given sentence, and the candidate must identify which one is opposite in meaning to the word named in the instruction.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The angles are equal, consequently the sides are ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. equal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "consequently" means as a result, therefore — it introduces a conclusion that logically follows from the previously stated fact.

• The sentence states a cause: "The angles are equal", and the blank must state the logical, corresponding effect. In geometry, when the angles of a triangle are equal, the sides opposite to them are also equal (as in an equilateral or isosceles triangle) — the two conditions go together.

• Since the cause (equal angles) and the expected effect must match in kind, the most logical word to complete the sentence is "equal".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "unequal" is incorrect because it contradicts the logical cause-effect relationship set up by "consequently" — equal angles cannot logically lead to unequal sides in this context.

• Option 3: "larger" is incorrect because it introduces a comparison that has no basis in the given sentence; there is nothing to compare the sides against.

• Option 4: "smaller" is incorrect for the same reason as "larger" — it introduces an unsupported comparison rather than the logical parallel implied by "consequently".

NOTE

• "Consequently", "therefore", "hence", "as a result" are all connectors used to introduce a logical conclusion or effect — the word/idea chosen after them must logically follow from what was stated before.

• Such fill-in-the-blank questions test comprehension of logical connectors as much as vocabulary — always check that the completed sentence makes logical sense, not just grammatical sense.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Like a cakewalk
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Easy task.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Like a cakewalk" means something that is very easy to do or achieve, requiring little or no effort. (बहुत आसान काम)
◦ Example: Winning the local quiz was like a cakewalk for her; she barely had to prepare.

• The expression originates from 19th-century African-American dance contests, called "cakewalks", in which the winning couple was awarded a cake for their elegant, seemingly effortless performance — hence anything done with ease came to be called "a cakewalk".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Smooth surface" is incorrect — it is a literal description, not related to the figurative meaning of ease of accomplishment.

• Option 2: "Pleasant experience" is incorrect because a cakewalk specifically emphasises the ease of a task, not merely that it is enjoyable; a task can be easy without necessarily being pleasant, and vice versa.

• Option 4: "Active" is incorrect — it describes a state of being energetic, which has no connection to the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• Other SSC-favourite idioms meaning "easy": "a piece of cake", "child's play", "a walk in the park", "as easy as ABC".

• Idioms meaning the opposite ("difficult"): "a tough nut to crack", "an uphill task", "a Herculean task".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.
After finishing high school, I plan to pursuing law.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. plan to pursue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "plan", when followed by another verb, must be followed by the to-infinitive (to + V1), not the gerund (V-ing) form.

• Rule: Certain verbs — such as plan, decide, want, hope, agree, promise, manage, refuse — are always followed by "to + base form of the verb". "Plan to pursuing" incorrectly uses the gerund "pursuing" after "to", which is grammatically wrong; "to" here is part of the infinitive marker, not a preposition.

• The underlined segment "plan to pursuing" must therefore be corrected to "plan to pursue".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No substitution" is incorrect because the original sentence contains a clear grammatical error — "plan to pursuing" is not a standard verb pattern.

• Option 3: "plan in pursue" is incorrect because the preposition "in" cannot follow "plan" in this construction, and "pursue" without "to" cannot directly follow "plan".

• Option 4: "plan to pursuing" is incorrect because it is identical to the erroneous original segment.

NOTE

• Verbs followed by to + V1 (infinitive): plan, want, decide, hope, agree, promise, manage, refuse, afford, learn.

• Verbs followed by V-ing (gerund): enjoy, avoid, finish, suggest, consider, admit, deny, postpone, practise.

• Some verbs can take either form with a change or no change in meaning, e.g. like, love, begin, start, continue.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Confusion
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Commotion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Confusion" means a state of disorder, uncertainty, or bewilderment; a noisy disturbance. (भ्रम/हलचल)
◦ Example: There was confusion in the hall when the lights suddenly went out.

• The word "Commotion" means a state of noisy, confused disturbance or excitement, which closely matches the meaning of "confusion" when it refers to disorder and chaos. (हलचल/शोरगुल)
◦ Example: The commotion outside the office turned out to be caused by a fire alarm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Intrepidity" means fearlessness or boldness (निडरता) — it is unrelated to disorder or confusion.

• Option 2: "Stagnation" means a state of not flowing or developing; inactivity (ठहराव) — it refers to a lack of movement or progress, not disorder.

• Option 3: "Perusal" means the act of reading something carefully (ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ना) — it has no connection to confusion.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "confusion": chaos, disarray, turmoil, bewilderment, disorder, pandemonium.

• Do not confuse "commotion" (noisy disturbance) with "promotion" or "emotion", which are unrelated words with similar spellings.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Our guests arrived; they are sitting in the garden.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. have arrived.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The second part of the sentence, "they are sitting in the garden", is in the Present Continuous Tense, showing an action happening right now, as a present result of the guests' arrival.

• Rule: When an action completed in the recent past has a direct, visible connection with or result in the present, the Present Perfect Tense (has/have + V3) is used, not the Simple Past.

• Since the guests' arrival has a clear present consequence (they are currently sitting in the garden), the underlined verb "arrived" (Simple Past) must be changed to "have arrived" (Present Perfect) to maintain tense consistency with the rest of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "shall arrive" is incorrect because it is Simple Future Tense, which contradicts the fact that the guests are already present and sitting in the garden.

• Option 3: "are arriving" is incorrect because Present Continuous here would imply the guests are still in the process of arriving, which contradicts "they are sitting in the garden" (an action that presumes they have already arrived).

• Option 4: "might arrive" is incorrect because it expresses future possibility, which again contradicts the fact that the guests have clearly already arrived and are seated.

NOTE

• Present Perfect Tense structure: Subject + has/have + V3.

• Present Perfect is commonly used with words/phrases like just, already, yet, ever, never, and — as here — to connect a past action to a present state or result.

• Do not confuse Present Perfect (result visible now) with Simple Past (action fully finished, with no direct link to the present).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
During an earthquake, / it is advised to take / cover above a table / to save your life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. cover above a table.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct expression for protecting oneself during an earthquake is "to take cover under a table", not "above a table". Taking shelter beneath a sturdy piece of furniture protects a person from falling debris.

• Rule — Preposition usage: The preposition "under" is used to indicate a position beneath or below something (used as protective shelter), whereas "above" means over or higher than something, which is the opposite and does not logically provide protection from falling objects.

• The segment "cover above a table" therefore contains the error — it should read "cover under a table".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "During an earthquake," is correct — it is a grammatically sound introductory prepositional phrase.

• Option 3: "it is advised to take" is correct — it is a grammatically sound passive construction ("it is advised") followed by the infinitive "to take".

• Option 4: "to save your life." is correct — it is a grammatically sound infinitive phrase of purpose.

NOTE

• Commonly confused prepositions of position: under vs above/over, below vs above, beneath vs on top of.

• "Under" is used for something physically beneath and typically providing cover/shelter, while "above"/"over" indicate something higher up, without contact.

• Related safety idiom often tested: "drop, cover, and hold on" — the standard earthquake safety advice.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hiest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the word is "Heist", meaning a robbery, especially one involving a considerable amount of money or property.

• Spelling key: H + EI + ST. "Heist" is one of the common exceptions where "ei" (not "ie") follows the initial consonant.

• The given option "Hiest" wrongly reverses the order of "i" and "e", making it incorrectly spelt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Finery" is correctly spelt — it means fine or elaborate clothes and jewellery.

• Option 3: "Cringe" is correctly spelt — it means to feel embarrassment or disgust and react with a slight cowering movement.

• Option 4: "Defer" is correctly spelt — it means to postpone or put off an action or event, or to submit respectfully to another's opinion.

NOTE

• Other common exceptions to the "i before e except after c" rule: weird, seize, either, neither, height, foreign, forfeit.

• Practise commonly confused word pairs with reversed vowel order, such as heist/hiest, receive/recieve, believe/beleive.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
All eyes
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Watching eagerly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "All eyes" means watching something very attentively and eagerly; giving one's full attention to something. (उत्सुकता से देखना)
◦ Example: The children were all eyes as the magician pulled a rabbit out of his hat.

• The expression uses "eyes" figuratively to represent complete visual attention — being "all eyes" means one's entire focus is on watching, out of curiosity or eagerness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Watching with anger" is incorrect — the idiom conveys eager interest, not any negative emotion like anger.

• Option 3: "Watching with no interest" is incorrect — this is the opposite of the idiom's actual meaning, which conveys keen interest, not indifference.

• Option 4: "Not watching at all" is incorrect — this directly contradicts the idiom, which specifically means giving full, eager attention.

NOTE

• Related body-part idioms of attention: "all ears" (listening attentively), "keep an eye on" (watch carefully/monitor), "eagle eye" (very sharp, watchful attention).

• Do not confuse "all eyes" (eager watching) with "turn a blind eye" (deliberately ignore something).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
He was looking into his book for the last two hours but couldn’t find it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. looking for his book.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "look into" means to investigate or examine something, which does not fit the context of a physical object like a book that cannot be found.

• The context of the sentence — "for the last two hours but couldn't find it" — clearly indicates that the subject was searching for the book, not investigating it.

• Rule — Phrasal verb usage: The correct phrasal verb for "searching for something" is "look for". The underlined segment must therefore be changed to "looking for his book" to convey the intended meaning of searching.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "looking down on his book" is incorrect because "look down on" means to regard someone/something with contempt, which does not fit the context of searching for a lost item.

• Option 2: "looking above his book" is incorrect because "look above" is not a standard phrasal verb with an established idiomatic meaning relevant here.

• Option 4: "looking after his book" is incorrect because "look after" means to take care of or be responsible for something, which does not match the context of trying to find a misplaced book.

NOTE

• Common "look" phrasal verbs: look into (investigate), look for (search), look after (take care of), look down on (despise), look up to (admire/respect), look forward to (anticipate with pleasure).

• Always match the phrasal verb to the exact context: "couldn't find it" is the strongest clue pointing to "look for" (searching).

question:
Select the most appropriate collocating word to fill in the blank.
Ram was praised for his________ leadership.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. visionary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A collocation is a natural combination of words that native speakers frequently use together; "visionary leadership" is a standard, widely recognised collocation referring to leadership that is forward-thinking, imaginative and inspiring in a positive, practical sense.

• The word "visionary" means having or showing clear ideas about what should happen in the future, especially in a way that is admired, which fits naturally with being "praised" for one's leadership.

• Applying the collocation rule: Ram was praised for his visionary leadership.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "imaginary" is incorrect because it means "not real, existing only in the mind", which does not collocate with "leadership" and would not be something one is praised for.

• Option 3: "magical" is incorrect because, although positive, it does not form a standard collocation with "leadership" in formal English usage.

• Option 4: "broad" is incorrect because "broad leadership" is not an established collocation and does not convey a clear, praiseworthy quality.

NOTE

• Other common leadership-related collocations: strong leadership, effective leadership, dynamic leadership, inspirational leadership.

• Do not confuse "visionary" (forward-looking, insightful) with "imaginary" (not real) — they look similar but have very different meanings.

question:
Select the most appropriate word segment for the underlined word in the given sentence.
Pintu has been advised to reduce smoking by his family doctor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. cut down.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "reduce" means to make something smaller in amount, degree or size; to decrease.

• The phrasal verb "cut down (on)" means to reduce the amount of something one does, eats, drinks or uses, and is the standard idiomatic phrasal-verb equivalent of "reduce" when talking about habits such as smoking.

• Applying the substitution: Pintu has been advised to cut down smoking by his family doctor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "less down" is incorrect because "less" is an adjective/adverb of quantity, not a verb, and "less down" is not a grammatically valid phrasal verb.

• Option 3: "lower down" is incorrect because "lower down" typically refers to a physical or positional decrease (e.g., moving something to a lower position), not reducing a habit like smoking.

• Option 4: "up down" is incorrect because it is not a meaningful phrase or recognised phrasal verb in English at all.

NOTE

• Other phrasal verbs meaning "to reduce": cut back (on), scale down, wind down, taper off.

• "Cut down (on)" is especially common when talking about reducing habits related to health, such as smoking, drinking, or eating certain foods.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Rebellion
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Loyalty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Rebellion" means open, organised resistance or defiance against an authority or established government. (विद्रोह)
◦ Example: The rebellion against the king's harsh taxes spread quickly across the province.

• The word "Loyalty" means faithful adherence and support to a person, government, cause or authority, which is the direct opposite of rebelling against that authority. (निष्ठा/वफादारी)
◦ Example: Despite the hardships, the soldiers showed unwavering loyalty to their country.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Uprising" means an act of resistance or rebellion; a revolt (विद्रोह) — this is a synonym of "rebellion", not its antonym.

• Option 3: "Sedition" means conduct or speech inciting rebellion against the authority of a state (राजद्रोह) — this is also close in meaning to "rebellion", not its opposite.

• Option 4: "Allotment" means the act of distributing something officially; a share allotted (आवंटन) — it is completely unrelated in meaning to "rebellion" and is neither a synonym nor a true antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "rebellion": revolt, uprising, insurrection, mutiny, sedition, insurgency.

• Other antonym pairs on the same theme: obedience ↔ defiance, allegiance ↔ treason, compliance ↔ resistance.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Hospitality
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Coldness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Hospitality" means the friendly and generous reception and entertainment of guests, visitors or strangers; warmth in welcoming others. (आतिथ्य/मेहमाननवाज़ी)
◦ Example: The villagers were known throughout the region for their warm hospitality towards travellers.

• The word "Coldness" means a lack of warmth, friendliness, or affection in one's manner towards others, which is the direct opposite of the warm, welcoming behaviour implied by "hospitality". (उदासीनता/शीतलता)
◦ Example: His coldness towards the new employees made them feel unwelcome.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Complaint" means a statement of dissatisfaction or annoyance (शिकायत) — it is unrelated to warmth or welcome and is not the opposite of hospitality.

• Option 2: "Cordiality" means warmth and friendliness in manner (सौहार्द) — this is actually a synonym of hospitality, not its antonym.

• Option 4: "Wrathful" means full of intense anger (क्रोधित) — while negative, it describes anger rather than the specific absence of warmth/welcome that is the true opposite of hospitality.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "hospitality": cordiality, warmth, geniality, friendliness, welcome.

• Related antonym pairs: generosity ↔ stinginess, warmth ↔ coldness, welcome ↔ rejection.

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of adverb of manner.
option_2: He has just done his work.
option_4: He has done his work on my table.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He does his work carefully.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An adverb of manner describes how an action is performed, and most such adverbs are formed by adding "-ly" to an adjective (e.g., careful → carefully).

• Rule: An adverb of manner is usually placed after the main verb or after the object of the verb, and it answers the question "How?" about the action.

• In "He does his work carefully", the word "carefully" correctly answers "How does he do his work?", making it a proper and correctly used adverb of manner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "He done his work regularly." is incorrect on two counts — grammatically, "done" cannot be used without an auxiliary verb ("has done"); and "regularly" is an adverb of frequency (how often), not an adverb of manner (how).

• Option 2: "He has just done his work." is incorrect because "just" here functions as an adverb of time, indicating when the action was completed, not how it was performed.

• Option 4: "He has done his work on my table." is incorrect because "on my table" is a prepositional phrase indicating place, not an adverb of manner.

NOTE

• Common adverbs of manner: carefully, quickly, slowly, happily, quietly, well, badly, beautifully.

• Categories of adverbs to distinguish: manner (how), time (when), frequency (how often), place (where), degree (to what extent).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Digital India can be the prime (1)_________ behind making a reality of the government's promise of minimum government, maximum governance. Such a transformation requires technology to be firmly (2)__________ into government, something that the Digital India project lists as one of its foremost objectives. Embedding technology into government (3)_________ will do three things; transform the government and make it more transparent and efficient, transform the lives of citizens especially those at the bottom of the (4)_________ pyramid and make our economy more efficient and competitive. A 2014 McKinsey Global Institute report predicts that the large-scale (5) _________ of technology through Digital India positions India with the biggest opportunity yet to accelerate economic growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. force.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that fits the collocation **"the prime ______ behind", meaning the main driving power or cause behind something**.

• "Force" fits perfectly here, since "prime force behind" is a natural, commonly used expression meaning the chief driving power responsible for bringing about a change or result — here, Digital India is described as the main driving power behind achieving "minimum government, maximum governance".

• Applying the fit: Digital India can be the prime force behind making a reality of the government's promise.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "impact" is incorrect because "impact" refers to the effect of something rather than a driving power "behind" an action; "the prime impact behind" is not an established or natural collocation.

• Option 2: "might" is incorrect because "might" refers to physical strength or power in a general sense, and "prime might behind" is not an idiomatic or natural expression in this context.

• Option 3: "factors" is incorrect because "factors" is typically plural and used with "among" or "one of", and "the prime factors behind" does not fit as smoothly as the singular "force" in describing a single unifying driving power.

NOTE

• Common collocations of "force": driving force, prime force, guiding force, unifying force — all behind/for a cause or change.

• In cloze passages, always read the full sentence (and often the surrounding sentences) to identify the collocation or idiomatic expression the blank is testing, rather than picking a word based on meaning alone.

solution_text:

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states that "technology" needs **"to be firmly ______ into government", and the passage later itself uses the related word "Embedding technology into government"** in the very next sentence — confirming that "embedded" is the intended word.

• "Embedded" means fixed firmly and deeply into a surrounding mass or system, which fits precisely with **"firmly ______ into government"**, conveying that technology must become an integral, inseparable part of the government system.

• Applying the fit: technology needs to be firmly embedded into government.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "inserted" is incorrect because "inserted" implies simply putting something into a system without necessarily becoming deeply integrated, which is a weaker fit than "embedded", and does not match the passage's own later use of "Embedding".

• Option 3: "planted" is incorrect because "planted" is typically used for physical objects (seeds, trees) or is used in an unrelated figurative sense (planting an idea); it does not collocate naturally with "firmly ... into government".

• Option 4: "stuck" is incorrect because "stuck" implies an object attached in a haphazard, temporary or superficial way, which contradicts the intended meaning of technology becoming firmly and deeply integrated into government.

NOTE

• Look for repeated or related words elsewhere in the passage (here, "Embedding" in the following sentence) — cloze passages are often internally consistent and give away the intended word choice.

• "Embedded" is commonly used in contexts of technology/systems integration, e.g. "embedded software", "embedded values".

A 2014 McKinsey Global Institute report predicts that the large-scale (5) _________ of technology through Digital India positions India with the biggest opportunity yet to accelerate economic growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. processes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"Embedding technology into government ______"**, referring to the internal working systems and procedures of government through which technology would be integrated.

• "Processes" means a series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular result; the established systems/procedures by which an organisation functions, which fits precisely with the idea of technology being embedded into how government actually operates and functions.

• Applying the fit: Embedding technology into government processes will do three things.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "offices" is incorrect because "offices" refers to physical locations or departments, not the functional systems/procedures that technology would be embedded into.

• Option 2: "details" is incorrect because "details" refers to small individual facts or particulars, which does not fit the idea of embedding technology into an operating system of government.

• Option 4: "hierarchies" is incorrect because "hierarchies" refers to the ranking/organisational structure of authority, which is a narrower and less fitting concept than the broader idea of "processes" through which government functions.

NOTE

• "Process" in a governance/technology context typically refers to the workflows, procedures and systems by which tasks are carried out — a term frequently used in e-governance literature.

• Distinguish "process" (a system of action) from "procedure" (specific steps within a process) and "policy" (a rule or principle guiding decisions).

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Such a transformation requires technology to be firmly (2)__________ into government, something that the Digital India project lists as one of its foremost objectives. Embedding technology into government (3)_________ will do three things; transform the government and make it more transparent and efficient, transform the lives of citizens especially those at the bottom of the (4)_________ pyramid and make our economy more efficient and competitive. A 2014 McKinsey Global Institute report predicts that the large-scale (5) _________ of technology through Digital India positions India with the biggest opportunity yet to accelerate economic growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. proverbial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"those at the bottom of the ______ pyramid", referring to the well-known economic concept of the "bottom of the pyramid"** — the largest, poorest socio-economic group in a population.

• "Proverbial" means referred to as if in a proverb; widely referred to as a well-known or common example/expression. It is commonly used right before an already well-established phrase (such as "the bottom of the pyramid") to indicate that the phrase is a familiar, standard expression, without literally meaning it is from a proverb.

• Applying the fit: transform the lives of citizens especially those at the bottom of the proverbial pyramid.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "mythical" is incorrect because "mythical" means existing only in myths or being imaginary/fictional, which contradicts the passage's intent — the "bottom of the pyramid" population is real, not imaginary.

• Option 3: "hypothetical" is incorrect because "hypothetical" means based on a suggested idea that has not been proven, whereas the "bottom of the pyramid" is a well-established, real economic term, not a hypothesis.

• Option 4: "classified" is incorrect because "classified" means officially categorised (or officially secret), which does not fit the idiomatic sense required before an already well-known phrase like "bottom of the pyramid".

NOTE

• "Proverbial" is frequently used in journalistic and formal writing right before a common idiom or well-known phrase, e.g., "the proverbial last straw", "the proverbial elephant in the room".

• "Bottom of the pyramid" (BoP) is a well-known socio-economic term referring to the largest, but poorest, socio-economic group globally.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. adaptation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"the large-scale ______ of technology through Digital India"**, describing how technology is applied and adjusted to fit large-scale use across the country.

• "Adaptation" means the process of changing something, or being changed, to suit a new purpose or situation, which fits the context of technology being modified and applied at scale to serve India's governance and economic needs.

• Applying the fit: a 2014 McKinsey Global Institute report predicts that the large-scale adaptation of technology through Digital India positions India with the biggest opportunity yet to accelerate economic growth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "enhancement" is incorrect because "enhancement" refers to an improvement in quality, not the large-scale application/adjustment of technology across a country described in the passage.

• Option 2: "anticipation" is incorrect because "anticipation" means expecting or looking forward to something, which does not fit the idea of technology actually being put to large-scale use.

• Option 4: "monitoring" is incorrect because "monitoring" means observing and checking something over time, which does not convey the sense of technology being widely applied at scale, as required by the sentence.

NOTE

• "Adaptation" refers to adjusting something to a new context, while the closely related word "adoption" refers to taking something up/starting to use it — both are frequently tested and easily confused in SSC vocabulary-in-context questions.

• In passages about technology and governance, look for words describing scale and application (adoption, adaptation, integration, implementation, deployment) as they commonly appear in Digital India / e-governance related cloze passages.
